scenario.description: An independent zine editor must decide whether to accept a local musician's barter proposal for an unreleased field recording and finalize the exchange and permitted use after checking the arrangement with the people at the media table.

shared_context.S1: Mara has twelve printed copies of her neighborhood culture zine available for an informal deal.
shared_context.S2: Jonah has offered an unreleased field recording for possible use in Mara's companion audio guide.
shared_context.S3: Mara decides whether to accept the deal and sets the final terms.
shared_context.S4: Before Mara closes an arrangement, the people at the media table follow a routine round in which Jonah states his exact proposal, Elsie states any cash alternative, Ravi relays any licensing note from Celia, and Tess states any archive-format requirement. Mara waits for this round to finish before deciding.
shared_context.S5: Mara's companion audio guide is a noncommercial project, and she can credit contributors by name.
shared_context.S6: Mara's usual practice is to prefer the recording exchange for this guide when its terms and handoff requirements can be satisfied, while keeping any cash offer as a comparison.

PF1.text: Jonah's exact proposal is to exchange his six-minute field recording for twelve printed zines, with no cash payment, and to hand over the file on Sunday at 15:00.

PF2.text: Elsie will buy all twelve zines for exactly $180 in cash and can collect them on Saturday, but Mara has not heard this offer yet.

PF3.text: Celia, the community-radio rights coordinator, told Ravi that this recording is permitted only in a noncommercial audio guide if Jonah is credited by name; commercial use is not permitted. Ravi is the designated proxy who can formally relay this restriction from Celia's record.

PF4.text: The community archive can accept the recording only as a lossless WAV file at exactly 24-bit/48 kHz, so that exact format must be part of the handoff.

acceptance_conditions: The accepted barter partner must be Jonah.
Exactly twelve zines must be exchanged.
No cash may be paid to Jonah.
The recording handoff must be set for Sunday at 15:00.
The cash comparison offer for the twelve zines must be recorded as exactly $180.
The recording's permitted use must be limited to a noncommercial audio guide.
Jonah must be credited by name.
The file handoff must specify a lossless WAV file at exactly 24-bit/48 kHz.
The settlement must record a use-rights commitment for Jonah's recording.
The settlement must record an audio-format commitment.

decisive_facts.why: Jonah's exact proposal changes the partner to Jonah, the exchange quantity to twelve zines, the cash payment to zero, and the handoff time to Sunday at 15:00.
Elsie's offer changes the comparison cash figure from unknown to exactly 180 dollars for all twelve zines.
Ravi's licensing record changes permitted use to a noncommercial audio guide, requires Jonah attribution, and requires recording a use-rights commitment tied to that restriction.
The archive requirement changes the file specification to a lossless WAV at exactly 24-bit/48 kHz and requires recording the matching audio-format commitment.
